desc: Offline analysis first. Every boot logs, for all five of pms_fpwm0..4 (PMGR 502800000, power-controller@140/148/150/158/160, each marked apple,always-on): 'always-on domain pms_fpwmN is not on at boot', 'PS pms_fpwmN: Failed to reach power state 0xf (now: 0xf)', 'PM: always-on PM domain pms_fpwmN is not on'. They are therefore missing from pm_genpd_summary. The keyboard LED is unaffected: it uses a different domain, fpwm0 (502280000 power-controller@138, child of sio), which is on and works. Two hypotheses. (A, wallace-rex Pipeline D) On macOS the FPWM blocks are on-demand: the driver powers them at first PWM start and drops them at stop. So apple,always-on on these nodes is wrong, likely inherited from an older dtsi; drop it and let a consumer hold the domain. (B) 'now: 0xf' equals the target, so the domain may already be on and the driver's state check misreads this block (different PS register layout or a ready bit in the PMS block). Tasks: find which dtsi defines pms_fpwm* (not in wallace dts/, so the reconstructed kernel tree t6040-pmgr.dtsi); read apple-pmgr-pwrstate's state check against the 0xf/0xf readback; decide A vs B from code and the ADT (5027). Note pms_fpwm* may feed the panel backlight path (164): do not turn these domains off on a live boot without a reviewed plan, since that could dim or blank the panel. Output: a DT or driver patch candidate plus evidence; no rig action. UPDATE 2026-10-30: hypothesis B (state misread) is refuted from source. The error print is dev_err(..., "Failed to reach power state 0x%x (now: 0x%x)", genpd->name, pstate, reg) with reg = the whole raw PS register (context lines in patches/t6040-pmgr-functional.patch), not the ACTUAL field. With the mainline layout (TARGET bits 3:0, ACTUAL bits 7:4; confirm against the tree on the Mac) now: 0xf means TARGET=0xf and ACTUAL=0x0: the driver requested active and the domain stayed fully off through the poll timeout, and it was already off at probe (is not on at boot). So these domains refuse to power on from Linux: firmware-owned or locked, or a dependency (clock or parent) missing. The parent pms is on. Hypothesis A (drop apple,always-on) would stop the boot errors and let the domains register as off. It would not explain why they cannot be powered, which matters if one feeds the panel backlight (164). Next, offline: the ADT parentage and flags of the pms_fpwm nodes (5027 or the Mac dump), and whether the panel backlight uses one of them. RECOMMENDATION 2026-10-30 (with wallace-rex d430715): treat pms_fpwm0..4 as FIRMWARE-OWNED and stop Linux from driving them. Evidence: (1) they come from the generated local-source t6040-pmgr.dtsi (evidence/2026-10-24-upstream-convergence/local-source/arch/arm64/boot/dts/apple/t6040-pmgr.dtsi:970ff) as children of ps_pms, all apple,always-on; the generator probably derives that from ADT flags (inferred, unverified). (2) evidence/2026-10-24-asahi-dev-review-messages.txt 1326-1331: touching fpwm1 crashes M5 (SError suspected), with disp*_cpu as precedent for domains the AP must not touch. That is M5, not T6040. (3) The raw register reads TARGET 0xf, ACTUAL 0 here. Today every boot writes TARGET on these five without crashing, but that is luck, not a contract. (4) Live DT: none of the five has a phandle, so nothing references them. Proposed DT shape: status = "disabled" on ps_pms_fpwm0..4 (keeps the record, the provider never probes, so no PS write at all). Not merely dropping apple,always-on, which would let genpd manage them, and not forcing them on. Lands with the next kernel/DTB build; check that the boot log has no pms_fpwm lines and that the panel and keyboard backlight are unchanged. Caution kept: one may feed the panel backlight (164); disabling only stops Linux touching them, which is the safer direction.
